bull.b: Repaying the major credit facility materially simplifies Soluna’s capital structure and releases liens on Dorothy project assets. Lower debt obligations can improve financial flexibility, reduce refinancing pressure, and support funding for renewable-powered AI and high-performance computing development.

A rapidly expanding renewable pipeline gives Soluna a broader asset base from which to scale energy-intensive computing. Combined with operating capacity expected to reach about 206 MW, this supports longer-term growth in hosting, AI infrastructure, and flexible power monetization.

The Applied Digital joint venture provides a concrete path to expand beyond cryptocurrency mining into AI and high-performance computing. Applied’s planned capital contribution and development role could accelerate deployment while strengthening Soluna’s position in renewable-powered digital infrastructure.

bear.b: Large net losses and compressed gross profit show that Soluna’s expanding infrastructure has not yet translated into sustainable earnings. New-site ramp costs, maintenance, and financing charges may ease, but the current economics still leave limited evidence of durable company-wide profitability.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means Soluna is consuming capital rather than funding growth internally. Continued cash burn can increase dependence on equity, debt, or project financing and may constrain execution if expected AI and renewable assets take longer to generate returns.

Expanded authorization and approval for potentially large equity issuance give Soluna financing flexibility, but they also create meaningful dilution risk. Additional shares could reduce existing holders’ ownership and per-share participation, particularly while operations remain loss-making and cash-consuming.
